# Cricket rule fixtures

cricket_golden.json is project-authored fictional data dedicated under CC0-1.0
(https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/). It does not reproduce a
real scorecard and does not assert realistic full-match tactics. The miniature
Test contains declared innings, the limited-over tie includes separate super
overs, and the abandoned match has no deliveries. Expected values are hand
calculated literals, not generated by the scoring implementation.

Test batting: eight sixes plus two = 50; ten sixes = 60. Thus two innings, two
fifties, zero hundreds and highest60, never a combined110. The other side scores
zero; draw is distinct from a tie/no-result.

Extras innings: wide1, no-ball+four5, byes2, leg-bye1, dot0, single+non-striker
runout1 = team10. Striker runs5, balls faced5; legal balls4; bowler runs7 and
wickets0. Super-over6 is retained in detail but excluded from career runs.
Retired hurt does not dismiss B; timed-out C and bowled A make two team wickets,
with one credited to the bowler. Empty abandoned innings contribute no events.

Rules and source-schema attribution: docs/SCORING_CONTRACT.md. Independent real
match checks are in tools/check_real_scorecard.py and docs/audit/real-scorecard-
2026-10-28.json; these require the local Cricsheet file and are not CI fixtures.
Cricsheet JSON is ODC-By1.0 (https://cricsheet.org/licensing/), not CC0. Its source
files/notices remain outside public assets. The CC0 dedication applies only to
the fictional golden data created in this project.

The penalty fixture starts on3 pre-innings runs, loses a wicket on3/1, and ends
on8 after5 post-innings penalty runs. The bowler concedes0 and completes a maiden.
Golden tests also replace a timed-out event with retired-out to check non-bowler
wicket credit. Legacy miscount strings normalize only with an explicit audit record.
